seo.metaDescription: Lost a loved one in Corte Madera? Our attorneys handle wrongful death claims for families in Marin County. Free consultation, contingency-based, no upfront cost.

hero.subtitle: When a death in Corte Madera was caused by someone else's carelessness, your family has a right to answers and to support under California law. We can help you understand your options and pursue a wrongful death claim in Marin County.

about.title: Corte Madera Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Corte Madera is a small town, fewer than ten thousand residents settled between the bay and the base of Mount Tamalpais, and when a family here loses someone, the absence is felt on quiet streets and in familiar places. Public records for 2025 show 48 injury collisions and 61 people hurt on local roads, with US-101, Tamalpais Drive and Paradise Drive carrying the largest share of reported crashes; those same records list no traffic deaths that year. Wrongful death claims in Marin County do not only follow collisions, though. They can arise from unsafe premises, medical mistakes, defective products and workplace incidents as well. Under California law, a spouse, domestic partner or child usually holds the first right to bring the claim, and a two-year clock begins on the date of death. The claim is civil, entirely separate from anything a prosecutor may or may not decide to do. Our team handles wrongful death claims on a contingency basis, so you can grieve while we track the deadlines and paperwork.

whyChoose.title: Why Corte Madera Families Choose Us

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing, giving a spouse, domestic partner and children priority before other dependents or heirs. We can tell your family quickly whether and how you qualify.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general filing window is two years from the date of death, and it shrinks considerably when a public agency is involved. We protect that window from the start.

items.title: Full picture of recoverable losses
items.desc: Beyond funeral and burial costs, California allows recovery for lost financial support and for the loss of love, companionship and guidance. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member was killed on US-101 near Corte Madera. Does the shorter government deadline apply?
items.answer: It might, and that is exactly why it is worth asking now. US-101 is a state highway, so if a road condition or public vehicle played a role, a claim against a government entity must be presented on a much shorter timeline than the standard two years. We can review the collision report and determine whether Caltrans, the Town of Corte Madera, Marin County or only a private driver is potentially responsible.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs on its own track, with its own deadline. The criminal case is brought by the state and does not compensate your family, while the civil claim exists to address your losses. Many families pursue both at the same time.

items.question: What does it cost to work with you?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. We handle wrongful death cases in Marin County on a contingency basis, which means no fee unless there is a recovery for your family.
